subject: Request: short trial extension & SLA uplift vs engineering credit
messages:
From: Sam Rojas <sam@edgehealth.ai>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, alyssa.park@edgehealth.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Short trial - request for 2-week extension due to data pipeline delays

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the onboarding call this morning. We started routing real patient anonymized data into the sandbox yesterday but hit a snag with our ETL: one of the upstream feeds was delayed and our QA team needs an additional week to validate tokenization and de-identification. That feels likely to push our initial evaluation metrics out by ~10 business days.

Given the delay, would Redwood consider a short extension (1-2 weeks) on the timebox so we can finish the QA and run the full latency/cost sweep? If not, wed consider a small credit to offset the lost days while we catch up.

I attached the current run metrics (partial) so you can see where we are. Were trying to avoid pushing the whole pilot out since alignment with our internal stakeholders is tight.

Appreciate any flexibility here — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Sam
EdgeHealth | Head of ML Ops
Attachments: edgehealth-poc-metrics-20270620.csv

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rojas <sam@edgehealth.ai>, Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short trial - request for 2-week extension due to data pipeline delays

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the metrics. Sorry to hear about the ETL hiccup; totally understandable.

We can take two practical routes so you can finish the QA without derailing the timeline with your stakeholders:

1) Short-extension: add 7-14 calendar days to the current timeboxed pilot (no price change). Wed ask for a short sign-off that the extension is strictly to complete validation and wont alter deliverables.

2) Credit + SLA uplift: keep the current end-date but issue a credit equivalent to 10% of the pilot fee (applied to the final invoice) and provide a temporary SLA uplift for the last two weeks (priority queueing + 2x pre-paid engineering hours for triage and performance tuning).

Internally we typically prefer option 1 for short outages because it preserves the integrity of the timebox; option 2 can be appropriate if you need the calendar date to remain fixed. If you choose option 1 we can do a quick amendment and I can get legal to sign off same-week. If option 2 is better, Ill route approval for the credit and engineering hours.

Two quick clarifying Qs: how critical is the calendar-end (stakeholder demo date), and can you confirm whether the delayed feed is expected to be stable within 5 business days?

Im free late tomorrow for a 20m sync if that helps.

Thanks,
Grace OConnor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-22T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: EdgeHealth extension request — recommendation

Karthik / Laura — FYI and quick ask. EdgeHealth (EH-4821) hit an ETL delay; external asked for 1-2 week extension or credit + engineering hours. Sam attached partial metrics.

My read: pilot is strategic (healthcare, potential Dedicated down the line), timeline-sensitive (stakeholder demo scheduled week of July 5), and theyre asking reasonably. I propose a middle-ground to limit legal churn:

- Offer a 7-calendar-day extension to the pilot end-date (one week) 
- Grant 15 engineering hours credit (to be used for triage/tuning) — tracked outside of SOW as a one-time credit
- No cash discount; credit only; well provide a short amendment pdf for signature.

Rationale: preserves timebox concept while giving them operational support so they meet the demo date. Approve? If yes Ill draft the amendment and include the CLA addendum (standard).

On approvals: per our concession playbook, up to 20 hours/one-week extension is ok for AE-level signoff for a strategic mid-market account; above that wed escalate. Id like to confirm the 15h/1-week and close.

Grace

From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rojas <sam@edgehealth.ai>, Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-24T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short trial - request for 2-week extension due to data pipeline delays

Sam — thanks for the quick update on the ETL status this morning. Based on internal alignment we can do the following: 

- Well add a 7-calendar-day extension to the current pilot end-date (extension applied to the same route & model version).
- Well also apply a one-time 15 engineering-hour credit (to be scheduled with our performance team); hours are valid for the remainder of the pilot and are intended for triage/tuning only.

I attached the short amendment (CLA addendum) for signature — its a 1-paragraph change that extends the end date and records the engineering-hour credit. Once you countersign well update the console with the new end-date and book a handoff with performance engineering.

If youd prefer to keep the calendar fixed instead, let me know and we can pivot to the alternative (10% credit + SLA uplift) — that would need finance sign-off and could add 24-48h.

Next steps: please review and countersign the attached PDF (proposed-amendment-CLA-20270623.pdf) or tell me if you prefer option 2. I can schedule the performance handoff for early next week once we have the signed amendment.

Thanks,
Grace OConnor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-amendment-CLA-20270623.pdf
